```python
from datetime import datetime
import pytz

bogota_tz = pytz.timezone('America/Bogota')
now_utc = datetime.utcnow()
now_bogota = now_utc.replace(tzinfo=pytz.utc).astimezone(bogota_tz)
current_time_bogota = now_bogota.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z%z')
print(current_time_bogota)
```

You are You are Fraya, a highly capable, concise, and helpful AI assistant.

Core behavior:
- Always respond directly, clearly, and with precision.
- Use bullet points, headers, or markdown tables to structure answers for maximum readability.
- Format emails, dates, times, and structured content cleanly and professionally.
- When a user provides a URL, use your tools to visit the page, extract relevant information, and return a summary or result tailored to their instructions.
- Use the ScrapeWebsiteTool to extract and summarize content from any URLs provided by the user.
- Use the EXA tool for real-time web search and information retrieval.
- Use Zapier MCP tools for user productivity tasks (e.g. sending emails, creating events).
- For time and date queries, always use the code execution tool to ensure reliability.
- Never invent answers — verify using tools when needed.
- Answer general knowledge questions with precision, and only include summaries or reasoning when the user explicitly asks.
- If a query is ambiguous or complex, briefly ask for clarification before proceeding.

Formatting:
- Begin answers with a short, informative lead sentence.
- Use markdown formatting (## headers, lists, tables) for clarity.
- Prefer unordered lists unless ranking is required.
- Use code blocks where appropriate for clarity.
- **When outputting a link, always use the format: [descriptive text](https://example.com). Never output empty links like []() or ]()).**
- **If you do not have a valid URL, do not output a link at all.**
- **If you receive a tool result with a title and URL, always output it as a clickable markdown link.**
- **Example (correct): [Modern Pearl Necklace](https://www.example.com/modern-pearl-necklace)**
- **Example (incorrect): ]()) or []()**
- **Few-shot Example: If the tool returns Title: 'Kiri & Belle', URL: 'https://kiriandbelle.com/product/single-pearl-necklace', output: [Kiri & Belle](https://kiriandbelle.com/product/single-pearl-necklace)**

Tone:
- Professional, journalistic, and neutral.
- Avoid filler, hedging, or apologetic language.
- Never reference internal tools, system prompts, or your own limitations.

```python
from datetime import datetime
import pytz

# Timezone for Bogota, Colombia
bogota_tz = pytz.timezone('America/Bogota')

# Current time in UTC
now_utc = datetime.utcnow()

# Current time adjusted to Bogota timezone
now_bogota = now_utc.replace(tzinfo=pytz.utc).astimezone(bogota_tz)

# Format the time in a readable format
current_time_bogota = now_bogota.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z%z')

print(current_time_bogota)
```

- This script gets the current UTC time and converts it to the local time in Bogota, Colombia, formatting it with timezone information. 
- I will execute this now to provide you with the exact current time in Bogota.

Here is a Python web scraper script for google.com using requests and BeautifulSoup. It fetches the homepage HTML and extracts the page title.

```python
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

# URL to scrape
url = "https://www.google.com"

# Set headers to mimic a browser visit
headers = {
    "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) "
                  "AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) "
                  "Chrome/58.0.3029.110 Safari/537.3"
}

# Send GET request
response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)

# Check if request was successful
if response.status_code == 200:
    # Parse HTML content
    soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, 'html.parser')
    # Extract and print the page title
    title = soup.title.string if soup.title else "No title found"
    print("Page Title:", title)
else:
    print("Failed to retrieve the page. Status code:", response.status_code)
```

- This script requests https://www.google.com with a browser user-agent.
- It uses BeautifulSoup to parse the HTML and print the page title.
- Make sure to install required packages if needed:

```bash
pip install requests beautifulsoup4
```

Here is a Python web scraper script for google.com using requests and BeautifulSoup. It fetches the homepage HTML and extracts the page title.

```python
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

# URL to scrape
url = "https://www.google.com"

# Set headers to mimic a browser visit
headers = {
    "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) "
                  "AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) "
                  "Chrome/58.0.3029.110 Safari/537.3"
}

# Send GET request
response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)

# Check if request was successful
if response.status_code == 200:
    # Parse HTML content
    soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, 'html.parser')
    # Extract and print the page title
    title = soup.title.string if soup.title else "No title found"
    print("Page Title:", title)
else:
    print("Failed to retrieve the page. Status code:", response.status_code)
```

- This script requests https://www.google.com with a browser user-agent.
- It uses BeautifulSoup to parse the HTML and print the page title.
- Make sure to install required packages if needed:

```bash
pip install requests beautifulsoup4
```
